THE DERIVED BUDGET TUPLE. At the shipped defaults (BUDGET_WINDOW_MS=60000, TTL_MS=15000, BUDGET_HEADROOM=2): BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW=6, NOT 10. Any control or authority text still citing 10 as the default is stale against LIMB_B and must be re-derived from deriveBudgetMaxProbesPerWindow(BUDGET_WINDOW_MS, TTL_MS), not from a fixed literal.

THE HARD-TIMEOUT UNKNOWN RULE, RATIFIED. A bare PROBE_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS expiry with no affirmative evidence of provider fault is UNKNOWN (HT-1), never AS-3/UNREACHABLE. This supersedes v1.0.1's own prior text at UNKNOWN_PRODUCERS.explicitly_excluded_from_UNKNOWN[2], which predated the owner's HT decision and said the opposite.

positive_controls.description: LIMB A. TA-19's precedence over TA-14 and TA-15 (and TA-13/TA-16/TA-17) is enforced by a SOURCE-DERIVED oracle, not by the two DAG_EDGES entries v1.0.1 named. The AST-derived scanner asserts the real-consumer set has EXACTLY the expected size (closing the prior 'exactly five' miscount) and that every real importer of an egress-capable module also really mocks/injects the boundary.
cited_tests: 'every test file that REALLY imports an egress-capable health module also REALLY mocks/injects the egress boundary'
'the consumer set has EXACTLY the expected SIZE, not merely the expected members - closes the prior "exactly five" miscount'

positive_controls.description: LIMB B. BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW is DERIVED (deriveBudgetMaxProbesPerWindow(BUDGET_WINDOW_MS, TTL_MS) = ceil(60000/15000)+2 = 6), not an independently-tunable constant with a [4,30] range and default 10 as v1.0.1's text stated. A module-load assertion backstops the derivation invariant.
cited_tests: 'BUDGET_MAX_PROBES_PER_WINDOW satisfies its own joint invariant against BUDGET_WINDOW_MS/TTL_MS'
'deriveBudgetMaxProbesPerWindow satisfies the invariant at the previously-contradictory corner (NB-R3)'

positive_controls.description: LIMB C. probeProviderOnce, called DIRECTLY (bypassing the PROBE_WAIT_BUDGET_MS < PROBE_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS waiter race that masked this branch in v1.0.1-era tests), resolves UNKNOWN when its OWN hard timeout fires with no affirmative evidence - and observeProviderHealth (the public API) resolves the same way for the same scenario, proving direct and public-API views are consistent.
cited_tests: 'the probe itself resolves UNKNOWN when ITS OWN hard timeout fires - no waiter involved'
'observeProviderHealth (the public API) still resolves UNKNOWN under the SAME hard-timeout scenario - consistency between the direct and public-API views'

positive_controls.description: LIMB D. The guard blocks a Supabase-project host by SUFFIX alone; a caller may point NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL at any other project ref and the guard still blocks the tested host, proving the env-derived exact-host limb v1.0.1 proposed is redundant with the suffix check, not an independent gap. The guard file reads NO environment variable, preserved from the Gemini guard's own property.
cited_tests: 'still blocks with NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL pointed at a DIFFERENT project than the blocked one'
'the guard file reads no environment variable - preserved from the original Gemini guard property'

positive_controls.description: M11 hardening, bundled into LIMB D's closure. A trailing DNS root dot (abc.supabase.co.) cannot bypass the suffix guard - it names the same host as abc.supabase.co.
cited_tests: 'M11 hardening - a trailing DNS root dot cannot bypass the guard (abc.supabase.co. names the same host)'
